cards.headline:
AI is hollowing out
the middle of design
cards.body: After years of a growing design process, an essay argues AI is now squeezing its middle into an hourglass shape.

blocks.x: For fifteen years, the design process kept growing while the time left for making the product kept shrinking. Anamol Rajbhandari argues the middle of that process — research reports, personas, journey maps, wireframes, handoff specs, workshops — is draining now, with the weight moving out to the two ends: deciding at the top, making at the bottom, like an hourglass.

That middle was buying agreement among a dozen specialists while money was cheap. Then the Fed raised rates eleven times between March 2022 and July 2023, and ChatGPT arrived in November 2022, giving companies both a reason and the means to cut it.

Research had already shown the artifacts standing in for something else: practitioners used personas almost only for communication, and in one Rolf Molich study seventeen teams reported 340 usability problems, none found by every team. An AI model now drafts the discussion guide and surfaces the tensions in a stack of transcripts in a minute.

A working prototype now takes an afternoon instead of a quarter, so making comes back to the designer. The far end — judging what deserves to exist — becomes the moat: a designer decides what is worth making, collaborates at speed, and then makes it well.
